objective: Build a reproducible independent BTS-to-ZTF-DR24 spatial-recovery pilot, preserve every candidate OID and angular separation, and distinguish filter-level and field/quadrant-level OID multiplicity without changing the production selector or scientific acceptance criteria.
previous_knowledge_consumed: Official IRSA DR24 HATS documentation states that ZTF object identifiers are defined per filter, field, and quadrant; multiple OIDs are not automatically false positives.
The official BTS explorer snapshot retrieved on 2026-11-02 contains 10,551 rows and is preserved with SHA-256 af2362275074ff4b6c70523b9db6f2d5991af16fdd8d76ed47520948eb788e82.
Initial 100-object BTS-to-DR24 pilot run 41488299913 returned 773 OID rows within 5 arcseconds and showed strong radius-dependent multiplicity.
The existing StarEmbed adapter requires a verified Hugging Face revision and five Parquet artifacts; its coordinate-recovery pilot remains separate and pending.
Schema-aware BTS-to-DR24 source-backed run 41525750067 completed 100 targets and 773 unique OIDs; the live Objects Table schema exposed field, ccdid, qid, and fid.
The DR24 Lightcurves HATS table uses an objectid index; Objects Table presence does not prove a light-curve row exists.
Issue #188 raw DR24 light-curve artifact shows OIDs are single-filter: 5/12 selected OIDs were zi-only; the other 7 produced single-band, 19/42-finite feature vectors.
The completed source-backed run 41527459598 queried the DR24 Lightcurves HATS objectid index for all 773 recovered OIDs and uploaded artifact 13184608092.

baseline.description: PR #246 is based on main at this revision. Frozen v0.2.0 model, feature set, class order, production selector, and scientific acceptance criteria remain unchanged.

correctness.before: The initial DR24 query selected oid, ra, dec, and filtercode only. It did not preserve field/quadrant provenance.
correctness.after: The schema-aware query captures field, ccdid, qid, and fid. The auditor distinguishes same-filter OIDs across partitions from same-partition multiplicity. In the 100-object sample, same-filter same-partition multiplicity was 0, 15, and 77 targets at 1, 2, and 5 arcseconds. The indexed Lightcurves lookup found 714/773 OIDs and 59 missing rows; all 773 available filter metadata pairs were consistent. Per-filter missing counts: zg 25, zr 23, zi 11. 87/100 BTS targets had at least one matched Lightcurves OID in both g and r.

reliability.before: Recovery reliability had not been measured with a source-backed DR24 Lightcurves index lookup.
reliability.after: One source-backed 100-target run found 714 of 773 OIDs in Lightcurves HATS and 59 without a row. Repeat-run stability, larger samples, and scientific photometry usability remain unmeasured.
reliability.reason: A single source-backed run provides partial evidence only; repeat-run stability, larger samples, and scientific photometry usability remain unmeasured.

reproducibility.before: The first auditor wrote per-object multiplicity and nearest separation only.
reproducibility.after: The query manifest records the 76-column HATS schema and SHA-256, code revision, runtime versions, and selected provenance columns. The auditor writes one row per OID with recomputed separation and available field/CCD/quadrant/filter provenance. Input and output hashes are recorded. The Lightcurves manifest records the 13-column schema and SHA-256 9114cbba3b014cab91193e225bcdebf2f89878c10a1bab890dd9e683aa5a23f9, objectid index, input/output hashes, code revision, and runtime versions.

scientific_validity.reason: The BTS pilot is a positional candidate-recovery diagnostic. It does not establish physical identity, a validated association radius, object-level precision, or recall.

measurement.trade_off: The 5-arcsecond cone is retained as a candidate-generation radius. A narrower radius is not selected as an identity rule. Field/quadrant provenance and a new source-backed run are required before interpreting same-filter multiplicity.

Evidence artifact 13184608092, ZIP SHA-256 84548734b39fa5e1639e6b06ed54d0630c23603b4c6a803b3e7c0935966de7e3. It contains the BTS raw and normalized snapshots, deterministic 100-target sample, 773 spatial OID matches, multiplicity audits, Lightcurves availability by OID and by BTS target, and manifests.
The Lightcurves HATS index lookup queried all 773 OIDs. It found 714 rows and 59 missing OIDs. All 773 filter metadata pairs were consistent; missing OIDs: zg 25, zr 23, zi 11.

Among 100 BTS targets, 87 had at least one Lightcurves OID in both g and r, 96 had at least one Lightcurves row, and 60 had Lightcurves rows for every recovered Objects Table OID. These are availability counts, not proof of adequate cadence or clean photometry.
The 714 found OIDs had 1–1850 epochs (median 56.5). The Lightcurves manifest explicitly states that row presence does not certify clean epochs, minimum cadence, or scientific usability.

root_causes: The first query did not select DR24 field, CCD, quadrant, or readout-channel provenance.
The first audit did not preserve one recomputed angular separation row per returned OID.
The initial 5-arcsecond cone includes many close OIDs. For one BTS source, 22 OIDs were returned within 5 arcseconds, but only one was within 1 arcsecond.
The DR24 Objects Table schema exposed field, ccdid, qid, and fid but not rcid; the available fields are sufficient to distinguish the sample's field/CCD/quadrant partitions.
The 5-arcsecond cone includes same-filter multiple OIDs within the same partition for 77/100 BTS targets; these are candidate nearby catalog objects, not automatically false positives.

The existing DR24 feature-engine smoke test selected filter-specific OIDs as if each OID were a complete astrophysical source. All 7 successful feature calculations were single-band and 19/42 finite; the 5 failed OIDs were i-only.
unresolved: Inspect quality flags, cadence, time coverage, and usable photometry for a stratified sample of the 714 OIDs with Lightcurves rows; row presence alone is insufficient.
Build and validate astrophysical source groups that map constituent OIDs across filters, fields, CCDs, and quadrants. Preserve ambiguity and all source IDs.
Re-run feature generation on combined g/r source groups. Require valid g/r coverage before model inference.
Inspect a stratified set of light curves and BTS transient positions before defining an association rule.
Resolve StarEmbed duplicate/overlap evidence before using its metrics.

findings: Multiple ZTF OIDs must not be counted as false positives without checking filter, field, and quadrant provenance.
The initial BTS sample recovered 48, 78, and 97 of 100 targets within 1, 2, and 5 arcseconds, respectively; the 5-arcsecond radius is not a validated identity threshold.
BTS type '-' is an unclassified placeholder and must not enter a labeled classification benchmark.
A passing synthetic contract suite does not prove the updated live DR24 association behavior.
The 1-arcsecond sample had no same-filter multi-OID cases within one field/CCD/quadrant partition; at 5 arcseconds, 77 targets did. This supports using the wider cone only for candidate generation.
The Objects Table may contain OIDs without corresponding Lightcurves rows; availability must be checked by the Lightcurves objectid index.
A DR24 OID is filter/field/quadrant-specific. The v0.2 g/r feature contract needs a grouped astrophysical source input, not a single-filter OID light curve.
The indexed Lightcurves HATS lookup found rows for 714/773 recovered OIDs; 59 OIDs had no row. This availability result is distinct from photometry-quality validation.
The 59 missing Lightcurves OIDs were 25 zg, 23 zr, and 11 zi. All 773 returned OIDs had consistent Objects Table and Lightcurves filter metadata when a row existed.
87/100 BTS targets had at least one Lightcurves OID in both g and r; 60/100 had rows for every recovered OID. Neither metric proves valid g/r feature coverage or astrophysical identity.

open_blockers: Source-group construction and g/r feature-engine integration remain unimplemented and require regression-backed validation.
Lightcurve photometry quality, cadence, and time coverage have not been scientifically audited.

knowledge_carried_forward: Do not equate BTS 9-character IDs with DR24 numeric OIDs; use coordinates only to generate candidate associations.
Do not interpret 5-arcsecond spatial matches as physical identity.
Require complete field/quadrant provenance before interpreting same-filter OID multiplicity.
Exclude BTS type '-' from all labeled classification evaluation.
Keep StarEmbed coordinate recovery separate from BTS transient recovery.
Do not modify the v0.2.0 production baseline or scientific acceptance criteria in this workstream.
Do not use a single DR24 OID as a complete g/r source input. Group its filter-specific OIDs under a traceable astrophysical source identity before feature generation.
Do not assume an Objects Table OID has a corresponding Lightcurves row; query the objectid index and record nepochs.
A 5-arcsecond cone is a broad candidate-generation radius; the 1-arcsecond result is promising but not an accepted identity rule.
